step1_summary.Chief complaint: Feeling anxious over the past few months, nervous every morning about leaving the house.
Symptoms: Onset: About 2 months ago, coinciding with starting a new stressful job.
Anxiety predominantly related to work and interactions with a difficult boss.
Morning palpitations described as irregular, lasting minutes up to 10 minutes, sometimes painful.
Difficulty falling asleep, waking early with racing heart, shallow sleep, approx 3-4 hours per night.
Low energy and motivation during the day, loss of enjoyment in usual activities.
Avoidance of socializing and hobbies due to anxiety and low mood.
No chest pain except transient discomfort associated with palpitations.
No panic attacks reported but fear that symptoms could be worsening.
Increased consumption of chocolate; appetite otherwise stable.
No suicidal thoughts but feels 'down' and worried about ongoing symptoms.
step1_summary.Past medical history: No mention of prior psychiatric diagnoses; mother has history of depression.
step1_summary.Family/Social history: Lives with retired parents. Mother has past depression. Social alcohol use, increased on weekends. Occasional smoking, no other drugs.
step1_summary.Vital signs/exam findings: No vital signs or physical exam findings documented.
step1_summary.Labs/Imaging: No labs/imaging done yet; provider suggested basic blood tests to rule out triggers.

V: Arrhythmia – palpitations associated with irregular fast heartbeat might suggest a cardiac arrhythmia possibly triggered or exacerbated by anxiety.
I: Thyroiditis or other infectious/inflammatory cause – could cause palpitations, anxiety, or mood changes.
D: Nutritional deficiency (e.g., iron deficiency anemia, B12 deficiency) – can contribute to anxiety, fatigue, and palpitations.
I2: Substance use or withdrawal effects – alcohol use, smoking, or caffeine could worsen anxiety and palpitations.
A: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) or Work-related Anxiety – suggested by chronic anxiety symptoms related to work stress.
Depressive disorder – low mood, anhedonia, and cognitive symptoms.
E: Hyperthyroidism – can cause palpitations, anxiety, insomnia, and low mood.
Other metabolic/endocrine disorders (e.g., pheochromocytoma) – less likely but possible cause of palpitations and anxiety.
